# /eval — Phase 7 calibration & evals

*This directory is the evidence. `eval/README.md` is generated by `make eval`
and holds the current numbers; this file explains what everything is and does
not change between runs.*

## Reproducing

```sh
make eval-fast     # analytic laws + rank agreement + report — seconds, no database
make eval          # everything, including the real scenario runs — needs a live HydraDB
make eval-clean    # delete generated artifacts (keeps specs and profiles)
```

`make eval` is deliberately slow: the scenario tier runs real simulations,
because a face-validity law proved on a special code path proves nothing about
the engine that ships. Per-tick cost grows with the store — if it crawls,
archive the store (`infra/README.md`) and retry.

## What is here

| path | what it is | generated? |
|---|---|---|
| `calibration.md` | 7.2 — what changed, why, before/after | hand-written |
| `market-research.md` | every published band with its source | hand-written |
| `profiles/reference.json` | the calibrated profile, certified against the bands | hand-written |
| `profiles/demo.json` | the accelerated profile, with its multiples published | hand-written |
| `specs/*.json` | one run config per scenario law (F4, F5, F7b, F9, F11, F12) | hand-written |
| `configs/reference.json` | the reference shape the calibration is certified on | hand-written |
| `configs/built/` | specs + profile merged into runnable configs | generated |
| `results/*.json` | every number the suite produced | generated |
| `plots/*.svg` | every chart | generated |
| `fixtures/quality-{good,bad}/` | F11's two catalogs, differing only in latent_quality | generated |
| `README.md` | the report | generated |

## The three tiers, and why

| tier | cost | what it carries |
|---|---|---|
| **analytic** | milliseconds, no database | F1, F2, F3, F6, F8, F10 · rank agreement · the whole calibration fit |
| **scenario** | real runs on the live store | F4, F5, F7b, F9, F11, F12 — the laws that only exist once learning, retrieval and the graph are in the loop |
| **audit** | free | F7a — an assertion over `provenance_coverage`, which Phase 6 already computes |

A law goes in the cheapest tier that can actually test it. F8 and F10 are
properties of one formula and need no population; F9 needs a real paired twin
run and gets one.

## Charts are SVG on purpose

Hand-written, dependency-free, deterministic. A PNG from a plotting library
varies with the library version, the font stack and the platform; this repo
hashes everything and `make eval` has to "reproduce every number and plot from
scratch". SVG diffs cleanly in git, so a calibration change *shows* as a chart
change in review.

## The two things this suite will not tell you

1. **The rank-agreement study is construct validity, not external validation.**
   The synthetic oracle reads the same population priors the simulator does. It
   is independent of the *mechanism*, not of the inputs. Agreement means the
   appraisal-and-gate pipeline preserves an ordering already implicit in its
   inputs; it is not evidence that either ranking matches a real market.

2. **Offline replay is first-order.** `shopsim.eval.calibrate` re-scores the
   contexts a baseline run produced. It cannot model the feedback loop where a
   better click rate teaches more preferences and raises relevance for every
   later impression. That is why fitted profiles are always verified on a real
   re-run, and why the predicted-vs-realised gap is reported rather than assumed
   away.

## Scope

F1–F12 are implemented. **F13 (habit), F14 (social on/off) and F15
(overpromise/LTV) are not** — they are P1 on PLAN.md's cut list and were
explicitly out of scope for this phase. 7.5 (LongMemEval) is PLAN's own stretch
item and was not attempted.
